# Selector Ownership Delta

The Awtsmoos renews the law that measures garments before the garment claims the blame;
Awtsmoos.com now distinguishes a real duplicate selector from a parser that fractured its name.

## Evidence

Focused verification reduced the reader to one ownership-test failure. Portal geometry and cascade architecture passed.

The remaining report contained:

- one genuine duplicate owner for `.awtsmoos-sidebar-shell`
- two false fragments created by splitting commas nested inside CSS `:is(...)`

Direct source reads proved the functional selectors were different:

- tokens own generic control typography through `:is(button, input, select, textarea)`
- settings controls own disabled state through `:is(button, select, input):disabled`

## Corrective architecture

- containment no longer owns the shell element itself
- selector-list parsing moves to `TiferesStyleGraphProbe`
- graph parsing splits only top-level commas, preserving functional selectors as one unit
- graph-wide duplicate-selector rejection remains strict
- no conflict is whitelisted merely to obtain a green result

NEXT_ACTION: structurally verify the probe/test rewrite, then rerun the focused ownership contract.
